g3ela-28-1-teach-morph: [curious] Look up at the night sky! Constellation. A constellation is a group of stars together in the sky. The front part, con, means with or together. Its twin, com, means the same thing. Read the four words, and tap See what was hiding. Then type each whole word.
g3ela-28-1-teach-vocab: Be a word detective with me. Uncombed. Here's the sentence. The children came out of the cave unbrushed and uncombed. One, read the sentence: they just woke up. Two, look for word parts: un, comb, e d. Three, check it. Uncombed means not combed. Read how we figured out the first word. Then fill in each sentence with a word from the word bank, and tap Check My Work. Last, play the matching game.
g3ela-28-1-teach-gram: [warmly] An apostrophe has two jobs. Job one: it joins two words. Can, plus not, makes can't. The apostrophe sits where the letters left. Job two: it shows belonging. The dog's bone is the bone that belongs to the dog. Tap Now check your thinking. Then find the five words that need an apostrophe.
g3ela-28-1-teach-spell: Three spelling changes, coming up! Swim, swimming: the m doubles. Bake, baking: the e drops off. Try, tried: the y turns into i. Think about the questions, and tap Now name the pattern. Then sort the words.
g3ela-28-2-teach-morph: Watch one match first. Companion. Find the front part: com. It means with. A companion is a friend who goes along with you. That's my match! Read the Remember box. Then tap a word, and tap what it means. Match all four words.
g3ela-28-2-teach-vocab: Ever seen a grin that made you want to look away? Repulsive. The dwarf grins at Edmund in a repulsive way. Repulsive means so nasty you want to turn away. Now tap a word, then tap its meaning. Match all four.
g3ela-28-2-teach-gram: Spot the apostrophe. Mrs. Beaver's sewing machine was too heavy to bring. Beaver's, with an apostrophe s, shows belonging. Find the apostrophes in each of the four sentences, and tap Now check your thinking. Then fix the paragraph.
g3ela-28-2-teach-spell: Detective question! Which of these doubled its last letter: fatter, or faster? Fatter! Fat has a short vowel and one t, so the t doubles. Read the rule. Then in each row, tap the one word that matches what the row asks for.
g3ela-28-2-teach-rwm: Let's try all three parts with a sentence from Chapter 11. The snow was again falling as they came into the courtyard, but she took no notice of that and made Edmund sit beside her on the sledge. Part one, read like a reader. The Witch doesn't care about the snow. Part two, read like a writer. Weather first, then but turns to the story. Part three, mimic. Here's mine: The rain was pouring as we left school, but Mom took no notice and made us run to the car. Now it's your turn with the sentence about the snow and the moon. Write one sentence in each box.
g3ela-28-3-teach-morph: Snap the parts together. Con. Tact. Contact! When two things are in contact, they touch together. Say each pair of parts out loud. Type the whole word in the box. Then tap Check My Answers.
g3ela-28-3-teach-vocab: Try each word in the blank, and keep the one that makes sense. Here's my sentence. After a long nap, my grandpa felt blank. Herald? Hmm, no. Renewed? Yes! Now pick the word that fits each sentence.
g3ela-28-3-teach-gram: Let's be the editor. The dwarfs whip wasnt kind to the reindeer. Dwarf's needs an apostrophe: the whip belongs to the dwarf. Wasn't needs one too: was, plus not. Read the before and after, and tap Check yourself. Then fix the sentence in the gray box.
g3ela-28-3-teach-spell: Let's build one. Hike, plus i n g. Hike ends in a silent e, so the e drops off. Hiking! Read the rule. Decide which change each word needs. Then tap the card to build the new word.
g3ela-28-4-teach-morph: Quick question: what do com and con mean? With, or together! Here's a word that's not on the dice. Community. A community is people who live together. Now tap Roll the Dice. Say what each word means, and tap Check My Thinking. Roll all six.
g3ela-28-4-teach-vocab: Here's how I'd use a word about the story. Solemn. Peter was silent and solemn when Father Christmas handed him a sword. One word, one moment. Now choose one of your words and write your own sentence about Chapters 10 to 12.
g3ela-28-4-teach-gram: Two passes, like an editor. mr beavers tail was the last thing lucy saw. Pass one, capitals: Mr., Beaver and Lucy. Pass two, apostrophes: Beaver's tail. Now do your passes, and tap every word that needs fixing.
g3ela-28-4-teach-spell: Here's my roll. Fry, plus e d. Fry ends in y after a consonant, so the y turns into i. Fried! Tap Roll the dice, decide which change the word needs, or none, and tap Check my answer.
